[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (2) The period for filing the completed bill is 14 days after the end of the detailed assessment hearing. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (3) When a completed bill is filed the court will issue a final costs certificate and serve it on the parties to the detailed assessment proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (4) Paragraph (3) is subject to any order made by the court that a certificate is not to be issued until other costs have been paid. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (5) A final costs certificate will include an order to pay the costs to which it relates, unless the court orders otherwise. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (Practice Direction 47 deals with the form of a final costs certificate.)

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.17] (6) Where the court issues a final costs certificate in detailed assessment proceedings pursuant to an order under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act, the receiving party must send a copy of the final costs certificate to the prescribed charity. ## 47.18

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (1) Where the court is to assess costs of a LSC funded client, an assisted person or a person to whom legal aid is provided which are payable out of the Community Legal Services Fund or by the Lord Chancellor under Part 1 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012, that person’s solicitor may commence detailed assessment proceedings by filing a request in the relevant practice form. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (2) A request under paragraph (1) must be filed within 3 months after the date when the right to detailed assessment arose. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (3) The solicitor must also serve a copy of the request for detailed assessment on the LSC funded client, the assisted person or the person to whom legal aid is provided, if notice of that person’s interest has been given to the court in accordance with community legal service or legal aid regulations. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (4) Where the solicitor has certified that the LSC funded client or that person wishes to attend an assessment hearing, the court will, on receipt of the request for assessment, fix a date for the assessment hearing. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (5) Where paragraph (3) does not apply, the court will, on receipt of the request for assessment provisionally assess the costs without the attendance of the solicitor, unless it considers that a hearing is necessary. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (6) After the court has provisionally assessed the bill, it will return the bill to the solicitor. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.18] (7) The court will fix a date for an assessment hearing if the solicitor informs the court, within 14 days after receiving the provisionally assessed bill, that the solicitor wants the court to hold such a hearing. ## 47.19

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (1) Where the court is to assess costs which are payable out of a fund other than the Community Legal Service Fund, the receiving party may commence detailed assessment proceedings by filing a request in the relevant practice form. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (2) A request under paragraph (1) must be filed within 3 months after the date when the right to detailed assessment arose. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (3) The court may direct that the party seeking assessment serve a copy of the request on any person who has a financial interest in the outcome of the assessment. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (4) The court will, on receipt of the request for assessment, provisionally assess the costs without the attendance of the receiving party, unless the court considers that a hearing is necessary. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (5) After the court has provisionally assessed the bill, it will return the bill to the receiving party. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.19] (6) The court will fix a date for an assessment hearing if the receiving party informs the court, within 14 days after receiving the provisionally assessed bill, that the receiving party wants the court to hold such a hearing. ## VII COSTS OF DETAILED ASSESSMENT PROCEEDINGS

## Liability for costs of detailed assessment proceedings

## 47.20

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (1) The receiving party is entitled to the costs of the detailed assessment proceedings except where –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (a) the provisions of any Act, any of these Rules or any relevant practice direction provide otherwise; or

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (b) the court makes some other order in relation to all or part of the costs of the detailed assessment proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (2) Paragraph (1) does not apply where the receiving party has pro bono representation in the detailed assessment proceedings but that party may apply for an order in respect of that representation under section 194(3) of the 2007 Act. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (3) In deciding whether to make some other order, the court must have regard to all the circumstances, including –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (a) the conduct of all the parties;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (b) the amount, if any, by which the bill of costs has been reduced; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (c) whether it was reasonable for a party to claim the costs of a particular item or to dispute that item. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (4) The provisions of Part 36 apply to the costs of detailed assessment proceedings with the following modifications –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (a) ‘claimant’ refers to ‘receiving party’ and ‘defendant’ refers to ‘paying party’;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (b) ‘trial’ refers to ‘detailed assessment hearing’;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (c) a detailed assessment hearing is “in progress” from the time when it starts until the bill of costs has been assessed or agreed;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (d) for rule 36.14(7) substitute “If such sum is not paid within 14 days of acceptance of the offer, or such other period as has been agreed, the receiving party may apply for a final costs certificate for the unpaid sum.”;

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (e) a reference to ‘judgment being entered’ is to the completion of the detailed assessment, and references to a ‘judgment’ being advantageous or otherwise are to the outcome of the detailed assessment. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (5) The court will usually summarily assess the costs of detailed assessment proceedings at the conclusion of those proceedings. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (6) Unless the court otherwise orders, interest on the costs of detailed assessment proceedings will run from the date of default, interim or final costs certificate, as the case may be. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.20] (7) For the purposes of rule 36.17, detailed assessment proceedings are to be regarded as an independent claim. ## VIII APPEALS FROM AUTHORISED COURT OFFICERS IN DETAILED ASSESSMENT PROCEEDINGS

## Right to appeal

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > Right to appeal] 47.21 Any party to detailed assessment proceedings may appeal against a decision of an authorised court officer in those proceedings. ## Court to hear appeal

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > Court to hear appeal] 47.22 An appeal against a decision of an authorised court officer lies to a costs judge or a district judge of the High Court. ## Appeal procedure

## 47.23

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.23] (1) The appellant must file an appeal notice within 21 days after the date of the decision against which it is sought to appeal. [PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.23] (2) On receipt of the appeal notice, the court will –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.23] (a) serve a copy of the notice on the parties to the detailed assessment proceedings; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.23] (b) give notice of the appeal hearing to those parties. ## Powers of the court on appeal

## 47.24 On an appeal from an authorised court officer the court will –

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.24 On an appeal from an authorised court officer the court will –] (a) re-hear the proceedings which gave rise to the decision appealed against; and

[PART 47 – PROCEDURE FOR ASSESSMENT OF COSTS AND DEFAULT PROVISIONS > 47.24 On an appeal from an authorised court officer the court will –] (b) make any order and give any directions as it considers appropriate. ## Footnotes
